name: max_flow_min_cut
author: 1e59ba80
description: Computes the maximum flow from a source node to a sink node (Edmonds-Karp) and the minimum cut: the cheapest set of edges whose removal disconnects sink from source. Use for questions like 'Where is the bottleneck between X and Y?', 'How much can flow from X to Y?' or 'Which routes would have to be cut to separate X from Y?'. Works on directed and undirected graphs (an undirected edge carries flow both ways). Capacity comes from edge weight by default (1 on unweighted graphs); use capacity='unit' to count edges, or a numeric edge attribute such as 'airlines' (in airports, weight is distance in km). Returns max_flow, the cut edges sorted by capacity (from source side to sink side), and the sizes of the two sides. Max flow 0 means no path exists.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

source.description: Exact id of the node the flow starts from; use lookup_node to find it from a name.

sink.description: Exact id of the node the flow ends at (must differ from source); use lookup_node to find it from a name.

capacity.description: What limits flow on each edge: 'weight' (edge weight), 'unit' (every edge 1, so the cut counts edges), or a numeric edge attribute name such as 'airlines'.
